title: MINOTAUR: Multi-task Video Grounding From Multimodal Queries

task_scope.task_family: video moment retrieval / video temporal grounding
task_scope.why_in_or_out: The task explicitly localizes query-relevant temporal moments or highlights.

background_setup.summary: # Introduction Fine-grained video understanding has emerged as a crucial capability for the development of augmented reality (AR) and robotics applications.

evidence.quote: # Introduction Fine-grained video understanding has emerged as a crucial capability for the development of augmented reality (AR) and robotics applications.

background_setup.summary: To achieve this level of video comprehension, an agent (e.g., virtual assistant) must be equipped with the ability to identify and reason about events and objects captured in videos, tackling a range of vision tasks such as activity detection , object...

evidence.quote: To achieve this level of video comprehension, an agent (e.g., virtual assistant) must be equipped with the ability to identify and reason about events and objects captured in videos, tackling a range of vision tasks such as activity detection [6, 69, 102], object retrieval [20],and (spatio-)temporal grounding [2, 9, 18, 32].

prior_work_summary.summary: Unlike prior work on long video understanding that relies on pre-extracted visual features , our model is fully end-to-end learnable and can be trained with partially annotated data, i.e., without requiring annotations for all tasks per video.

evidence.quote: Unlike prior work on long video understanding that relies on pre-extracted visual features [94, 99, 39], our model is fully end-to-end learnable and can be trained with partially annotated data, i.e., without requiring annotations for all tasks per video.

prior_work_limitation.summary: current research on video understanding has focused primarily on training individual, highly specialized models using task-speciﬁc annotated datasets , without considering the synergies between multiple tasks and the model’s generalization to novel tasks.

evidence.quote: However, current research on video understanding has focused primarily on training individual, highly specialized models using task-speciﬁc annotated datasets [6, 18, 21, 30, 64, 98], without considering the synergies between multiple tasks and the model’s generalization to novel tasks.

prior_work_limitation.summary: While the idea of building a uniﬁed framework for multiple tasks is conceptually straightforward, it does come with a number of core technical challenges.

evidence.quote: While the idea of building a uniﬁed framework for multiple tasks is conceptually straightforward, it does come with a number of core technical challenges.

evidence.quote: The ﬁrst challenge is the inconsistent input (visual, lingual)/output (spatial, temporal) format and output distribution across different tasks.

prior_work_limitation.summary: In addition, effective training of models that capture multimodal information across tasks without compromising per-task performance remains an open challenge .

evidence.quote: In addition, effective training of models that capture multimodal information across tasks without compromising per-task performance remains an open challenge [49, 83].

prior_work_limitation.summary: To address the challenges arising from inconsistent output distribution in long videos, we design a sliding-window based training and inference regime, combined with a foreground frame prediction module capable of generalizing across different tasks.

evidence.quote: To address the challenges arising from inconsistent output distribution in long videos, we design a sliding-window based training and inference regime, combined with a foreground frame prediction module capable of generalizing across different tasks.

core_problem_transition.summary: In this paper, we seek an alternative approach – building a uniﬁed framework for multiple ﬁne-grained video understanding tasks.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we seek an alternative approach – building a uniﬁed framework for multiple ﬁne-grained video understanding tasks.

core_problem_transition.summary: Taking the three episodic memory tasks as an example, the input of natural language query (NLQ) is free-form language and the output spans < 2 seconds, while the input of visual query (VQ) is an image crop and the output of moment query (MQ) typically spans >...

evidence.quote: Taking the three episodic memory tasks [20] as an example, the input of natural language query (NLQ) is free-form language and the output spans < 2 seconds, while the input of visual query (VQ) is an image crop and the output of moment query (MQ) typically spans > 1 minute.

method_transition.summary: In light of this, we present MINOTAUR, a uniﬁed multitask model that is designed to accept long videos and multimodal queries as input, and generate diverse structured outputs.

evidence.quote: In light of this, we present MINOTAUR, a uniﬁed multitask model that is designed to accept long videos and multimodal queries as input, and generate diverse structured outputs.

method_transition.summary: Foremost, we propose MINOTAUR, a uniﬁed, Transformer-based model for grounding multi-modal queries in long-form videos.

evidence.quote: Foremost, we propose MINOTAUR, a uniﬁed, Transformer-based model for grounding multi-modal queries in long-form videos.

method_transition.summary: In service of this model, we propose efﬁcient, multi-task training and inference strategies, which enable training with ﬁxed duration, partially annotated video segments, and testing on variable-length, long-form videos.

evidence.quote: In service of this model, we propose efﬁcient, multi-task training and inference strategies, which enable training with ﬁxed duration, partially annotated video segments, and testing on variable-length, long-form videos.
